hints: Focus on what an electronic configuration really tells you, the total number of electrons, which equals the proton number for an atom.
Add up the superscripts for each configuration to get 11, 17, 23 and 26, then recall that Na is 11 and Cl is 17.
Check the last two configurations against vanadium with proton number 23 to spot which one has too many electrons to be vanadium.
walkthrough:
**Count electrons to find proton number**

For a neutral atom, total electrons equals atomic (proton) number. Just add all the superscripts.

$$\text{total electrons} = \text{sum of superscripts}$$

**Identify sodium and chlorine**

Option A has $2+2+6+1 = 11$ electrons, so $Z = 11$ which is sodium, $\text{Na}$. Option B has $2+2+6+2+5 = 17$ electrons, so $Z = 17$ which is chlorine, $\text{Cl}$.

**Identify vanadium and spot the odd one out**

Vanadium has $Z = 23$. Option C has $2+2+6+2+6+3+2 = 23$ electrons, so it is vanadium, $\text{V}$ with configuration $[\text{Ar}]3\text{d}^34\text{s}^2$. Option D has $2+2+6+2+6+6+2 = 26$ electrons, so $Z = 26$ which is iron, $\text{Fe}$, not one of the three named elements.

options.A: Incorrect. $1\text{s}^22\text{s}^22\text{p}^63\text{s}^1$ has 11 electrons, matching atomic number 11, sodium. This is one of the three named elements, so it is not the odd one out.
options.B: Incorrect. $1\text{s}^22\text{s}^22\text{p}^63\text{s}^23\text{p}^5$ has 17 electrons, matching atomic number 17, chlorine. This is one of the three named elements.
options.C: Incorrect. $1\text{s}^22\text{s}^22\text{p}^63\text{s}^23\text{p}^63\text{d}^34\text{s}^2$ has 23 electrons, matching atomic number 23, vanadium. Students sometimes miscount the d electrons, but $3\text{d}^34\text{s}^2$ is correct for V.
options.D: Correct. $1\text{s}^22\text{s}^22\text{p}^63\text{s}^23\text{p}^63\text{d}^64\text{s}^2$ has 26 electrons, matching atomic number 26, iron ($\text{Fe}$). This does not belong to chlorine, sodium or vanadium, so it is the atom of another element.
